title: Street Tree Stormwater parameters
$comment: Percentages are stored as percent (15, not 0.15) so the readout and the stored value agree. Slider granularity is x-step, not multipleOf; see bathtub/schema.json for why.

year.title: Year
year.description: The run starts from the 2015 census and goes one year at a time to 2045. Deaths and plantings happen at the end of each year, so 2015 is always the census as recorded.

view.title: Show
view.description: Each tree is drawn as a circle the size of its crown, colored by the stormwater it catches in the year shown. The block view adds up the trees standing in each 2010 census block.

show_sites.title: Planting sites and losses
show_sites.description: Draws the planting sites not yet planted as open circles, and the trees that have died during the run as gray dots.

rain_in.title: Rainfall
rain_in.description: Rain in a year. The default is the 41.0 inches recorded at JFK in 2000, the year i-Tree uses for the Northeast ([Northeast Community Tree Guide](https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/28759), p. 100). The same rainfall is used for every year of the run. The range is ours.

interception_pct.title: Interception
interception_pct.description: The share of the rain over a crown that the crown catches. The default is the 15% measured on a Callery pear in Davis, California; a cork oak in the same study caught 27% ([Xiao et al. 2000](https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/61750)). The same share is used for every tree. The range is ours.

death_young_pct.title: Deaths, trees under 5 years
death_young_pct.description: The share of young trees that die each year. The default is the Northeast guide's figure ([Northeast Community Tree Guide](https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/28759), p. 94).

death_old_pct.title: Deaths, trees 5 years and older
death_old_pct.description: The share of older trees that die each year. The default is the Northeast guide's figure (p. 94). A tree's age is estimated from its trunk diameter.

plantings.title: New plantings
plantings.description: Trees planted each year on the 621 sites the census recorded as dead trees or stumps, chosen at random. Every new tree is a honeylocust with a 3-inch trunk. A site stays taken once planted, and a tree that dies during the run does not open a new site, so at 100 a year the sites run out after seven years.

draw.title: Random draw
draw.description: Which trees die and which sites are planted first are chosen at random. Each number is a different set of random choices. The same number always gives the same run.
